question.problem:
$$ A=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 3 \\ -1 & -3\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2\end{aligned}],\,y=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]. $$ Given the matrices above, write $A{x}^{T}⊙(y+{x}^{T})$ as a matrix product.
$A{x}^{T}⊙(y+{x}^{T})=\,\,$ {{field-1}} $0$ $-5$
$0$ {{field-2}} {{field-3}}
question.worked_solution:
The Hadamard product of two compatible vectors $u$ and $v$ can be expressed as the matrix product

$$
v⊙u=\text{diag}(v)u.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
A{x}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 3 \\ -1 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 8\end{aligned}]
$$

and

$$
y+{x}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that they are of the same size; hence, their Hadamard product is well-defined. We conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}A{x}^{T}⊙(y+{x}^{T}) & =\text{diag}(A{x}^{T})(y+{x}^{T}) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
